site.name: Griefcase
site.tagline: Leave it here. Feel a little lighter.
site.description: Griefcase is a private, anonymous space to write down what's weighing on you, leave it there, and feel a little lighter. Not therapy. Not a social network. Just somewhere to put things down.

hero.eyebrow: A quiet place for what you're carrying
hero.headline: Some things are easier to leave here.
hero.subcopy: Your thoughts don't need to make sense. They just need somewhere to go.

howItWorks.headline: There's no right way to use this.
howItWorks.intro: But if it helps, here's roughly how it goes.

steps.title: Open the case
steps.body: No sign-up, no explanation. Just a quiet page and a blank space.

steps.title: Write, or say it out loud
steps.body: Type it, ramble it, leave it half-finished. Or record a thought instead.

steps.title: Fold it and let it go
steps.body: Watch it become something you can put down — not something you have to keep holding.

steps.title: Leave it in the Griefcase
steps.body: It stays here, privately, if you ever want to see it again. You don't have to.

why.headline: You don't have to carry everything.
paragraphs: Some thoughts don't have anywhere to go. They're too heavy for a text message, too unfinished for a journal, too honest for a conversation you're not ready to have.

Griefcase isn't therapy, and it isn't trying to fix anything. It's just somewhere to put things down for a while — the anger you didn't say out loud, the grief that doesn't have an occasion, the sentence you keep almost sending.
Some thoughts aren't meant to be solved. Some days you just need somewhere to put them.

quote.text: You are allowed to feel this. You don't have to explain it to anyone — not even to us.

vision.headline: Presence first. Solutions only if you want them.
vision.intro: Griefcase today is exactly what you're using right now: a private space to write and let go, held only in your own browser. The thinking behind it is bigger than that, and it's honest to say so out loud.
paragraphs: Griefcase started from lived grief — from noticing that most people don't want a diagnosis on day one. They want to be heard before anything else. Support that adapts to a person, instead of asking the person to adapt to a system.

The longer-term idea is a layered space that only ever goes as deep as you choose: reflective writing and listening; optional peer support; trained volunteers; and, when it's genuinely wanted, licensed professionals. Every step up would be something you choose — never something a system decides for you.

layers.title: Reflection
layers.body: A space to think out loud — private writing today, and eventually a gentle AI presence that reflects rather than diagnoses.

layers.title: Peer support
layers.body: Optional, moderated company from people who understand, for whenever you want it.

layers.title: Trained volunteers
layers.body: Real people, trained to listen, for moments that ask for more than reflection.

layers.title: Professional care
layers.body: A clear, consent-based path to licensed support — never forced, never assumed on your behalf.

vision.note: Only the first layer — private writing and voice notes — exists in this version. The rest is roadmap, not a promise with a date. When any of it ships, it will be opt-in, clearly labeled, and never a stand-in for emergency care.

prompts.headline: Emotional prompts
prompts.intro: You never have to use these. Sometimes a starting line makes it easier.
rotating: Say the thing you couldn't say.
Write the message you won't send.
You don't have to make it beautiful.
Say it exactly how it felt.
cards: Write the text you're never going to send.
What are you tired of holding?
Say the thing you'd only say once.
What would you tell them if there were no consequences?
Describe the day it changed, if you can.
What are you still angry about?

library.headline: What I've left here.
library.intro: Everything you leave stays quietly in this browser, on this device. Read it back whenever you want. Or don't.
library.emptyBody: Whatever you leave will stay here, quietly, whenever you're ready to look at it again.

privacy.headline: Your thoughts belong to you.

points.title: Private by design
points.body: In this version of Griefcase, what you write is stored only in your own browser, on this device. It isn't sent to a server, and we don't read it.

points.title: Anonymous by default
points.body: There's no account, no email, no name required. There's nothing here that identifies you unless you choose to add it yourself.

points.title: Yours to keep or delete
points.body: You can clear anything you've left here at any time. Closing or clearing your browser will remove it too — nothing is kept anywhere else.

privacy.disclaimer: Griefcase is a space for private expression and reflection. It isn't therapy, medical care, or crisis support, and it isn't a substitute for professional help.

safety.label: If you're in immediate danger
safety.body: If you or someone you know may be in immediate danger, please contact your local emergency number, or reach a crisis line where you live. findahelpline.com lists helplines by country if you're not sure where to start.

about.headline: A room, not a solution.
paragraphs: Griefcase was built on a simple idea: not every thought needs an audience, an answer, or a fix. Sometimes it just needs somewhere to exist outside of you for a while.
We're not a therapy platform, a social network, or a productivity app. We're closer to a drawer, a shoebox, a case you can close. A small, private container for the things you're carrying.
If Griefcase gives you five quieter minutes in a hard day, it's done its job.

faq.q: Is anyone reading what I write?
faq.a: No. In this version of Griefcase, nothing you write leaves your browser. There's no one on the other end reading it.
No. Griefcase is a space for private expression, not treatment, diagnosis, or crisis support. If you're looking for professional support, a therapist or counselor is a better place to start.

faq.q: Can I lose what I've written?
faq.a: Since entries are stored only in this browser, clearing your browser data, using a different device, or using private/incognito mode will mean they don't appear. There's no account to recover them from.

faq.q: Do I have to write something 'good'?
faq.a: No. Half-sentences, fragments, and things that don't make sense out loud are all welcome here.
